column19: 180 cm, enters through the top (y face 3.8 cm) near the back and stops at (-31.6, 542.7, 334.4): d_face 63.3 cm (y), 29.1 cm from the cathode, 103 cm past the APA seam, 326 cm from the anode, in APA2 but at its top, far from the y<60 corner. Not isochronous (|dx|/L = 0.32). The profile sits on a ~5.5-6e4 plateau and climbs steadily over the last ~15 cm, 8e4 -> 9-10e4 -> 1.15-1.23e5 in the last 3 cm, riding just above the muon reference curve with no collapse: a clean Bragg rise, pin left at the fit end. Nothing is attached at the stop: all three azimuths show the track ending at the star with no arm or stub, and no row within 35 cm past it, so no undershoot candidate. Two isolated 2-point specks: 287016 at 35.4 cm (cos_fwd 0.12, 34 cm off the body line) and 286015 at 41.5 cm (cos_fwd 0.53, 28 cm off the line), both compact and detached: capture gammas, which on an STM_ONLY count in any direction. f_meas (stop = high-time end, ~slice 487): U, V and W charge end there; the two specks show as lone cells; the V (5597) and W (8888) dead bands are well away. 55011 is a delta 107 cm back on the body: delta / other.

column19: About 144 cm; enters through the top 2.7 cm from y = 606 and stops at (336.2, 498.2, 356.8): 21.8 cm from the anode face (nearest), 108 cm below the top, 334 cm from the cathode, 126 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. dQ/dx: plateau ~5-6.5e4 (ragged, one pair at 9.5e4 near 20 cm), 5-8e4 over the last 10 cm, then a textbook Bragg rise over the last ~2 cm (1.06e5 -> 1.23e5 -> 1.52e5 -> 1.63e5 -> 1.75e5 at the last point), sitting on the muon reference curve and peaking at the fit end: no overshoot (no peak-then-collapse) and the pin stays. No forward piece leaves the fit end, so no hot tip. f_meas: the track ends cleanly in all three planes, no dead channel at the end. 299040 (5 points, 2.4 cm, faint at 4452) sits 16.2 cm from the stop at cos_fwd 0.2, about 16 cm off the body line, with a clean charge-free gap to the stop in all three 3-D azimuths and in f_meas (W 9573 vs the track end at ~9538, same time slice): detached and compact, so gamma not michel under the attachment tie-break; a capture gamma on this STM_ONLY. 111016 (chain delta ray, 9.4-14.4 cm, cos_fwd -1.0) leaves the body at the 111014/111034 vertex 9.4 cm back and hugs the body line (~2 cm off it), its charge falling from 5e4 to ~0 going out: delta / other. The other seven pdg-13 rows are the muon body up to the top entry.

62 cm chain, enters through the top 6.3 cm from y=606 and stops at (24.0, 548.4, 53.6), 53.4 cm from the nearest face (z), 21.5 cm from the cathode and 177 cm from the APA seam, in APA1 (x>0, z<231). The profile sits on a ragged plateau of about 5e4 (dips to 2e4 at s 15-20) and climbs over the last ~8 cm to 1.35e5 at s~2.5 along the muon reference curve, with the last points still ~1.0e5; the droop from the peak to the last point stays far above the plateau, so it is ordinary scatter, not an overshoot collapse, and the pin stays at the fit end. The hot 2.5 cm piece 97012 (1.1e5) is on the chain, cos_fwd -0.99: the Bragg peak itself, not a hot tip past the end. A 10 cm arm (97011 8.4 cm + 97001 1.7 cm, d 0-7.4, cos_fwd 0.43) leaves the stop at plateau charge (5.5-6.0e4), hooking off the muon line in all three azimuths; a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is the Michel. Four small pieces 17-41 cm out, all 16-35 cm to +x of the body line on the Michel side, stepping down in time in f_meas away from the Michel: 279007 and 280008 (along the Michel direction) and 282010 are gamma; 281009 is +35 cm in x like the Michel but -22 in z (cos_fwd -0.36), called gamma, arguable. No dead channels at the stop in f_meas.

201 cm single-segment chain, enters through the top 12.9 cm from y=606 and stops at (51.6, 408.8, 302.5), 160 cm from the nearest face, 49 cm from the cathode and 71.5 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. The profile rides a ragged 4-6e4 plateau (dip to 3.7e4 at s 31-35), bumps to ~9e4 at s 7-9 and climbs to ~1.2e5 (about 2x plateau) over the last 2-3 cm, on the muon curve; short but a real rise, and the last point sits at the peak, so no overshoot. A 10.8 cm arm 142003 (d 0-10.2, cos_fwd 0.81) leaves the stop at plateau charge (4-8.5e4, no climb at its far end): in f_meas the track reverses direction in time slice at the stop in U, V and W, and in the c azimuth the arm bends ~60 deg off the muon line. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so the arm is the Michel; not a hot tip (10 cm at plateau, not a couple of cm at several times it). 348001 (2 points, 12.6-12.9 cm, cos_fwd 0.68) sits on the Michel line 2.5 cm past its end: tagged michel as the electron continuation across a small break; gamma would be the alternative. 350002 is a 2-point speck 54 cm back up the muon side, ~20 cm off the body line, opposite the Michel direction: delta / other. No dead channels at the stop in any plane (W dead bands are 100+ channels away).

50 cm track entering 7.4 cm inside the back face at (67.8, 142.2, 454.9) and ending at (72.3, 101.9, 436.1), 26 cm from the nearest face (z), 94 cm above the floor, 72 cm from the cathode and 205 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. dy = -40 over a 45 cm chord, so the fit end is the lower end, consistent with a downgoing cosmic. Clear Bragg rise: plateau ~5.5-7e4, points at ~1.05-1.1e5 at 7-8 cm, then the last 2 cm climb along the muon curve to 1.2, 1.33, 1.5 and 1.65e5 at the last point. No collapse, so the pin stays. Nothing continues past the stop in the 3-D azimuths or in f_meas; the grey tracks in W and U cross elsewhere. The only activity at the stop is two compact 2-point clumps, 295004 and 296005, both 3.2-3.3 cm from the stop on opposite sides of it (cos_fwd 0.53 and -0.14), reading 9.3e4 and ~3.2e4. Within 5 cm a compact piece counts as the Michel even across a gap (rule 13), so they are the Michel. They have size 0.0, which the degenerate-row rule would call delta / other, so the Michel rests on very little charge. Three specks 52-58 cm out in the forward hemisphere (293002 cos_fwd 0.71, 294003 0.31, 297006 0.68), past the stop and clear of the body, are tagged gamma; they are faint and uncertain. 292001 (2.7 cm, 26.7 cm out, cos_fwd -0.27, slightly backward and ~26 cm off the body line) is off in an unrelated direction: delta / other.

column17: mu- 700 MeV(gamma 19 MeV(e- 19 MeV), mu- 7.38 MeV)
column19: 304 cm track entering 18.6 cm below the top face, fit end in APA3 at (21.7, 307, 365): 97 cm from the nearest face, 134 cm from the APA seam, 19 cm from the cathode. The end view shows the last ~110 cm running at constant x ~20 cm (near-isochronous lower section, horizontal in U and V of f_meas), so it runs parallel to the cathode rather than into it. The profile climbs cleanly: plateau ~4.5-5e4 at s=25-45 cm, ~7-8.5e4 over 5-20 cm, ~9.5-9.9e4 in the last 2 cm, following the muon curve shape - a clear Bragg rise to ~2x plateau. From the stop vertex a ~15 cm arm (107002 1.4-6.6 cm and 107003 6.6-15.4 cm, both shower-typed, cos_fwd -0.55/-0.77) leaves at an angle down and back beside the body; the d azimuth shows it clearly separated from the body line: the Michel. 107007 is a 2 cm piece at the vertex whose charge falls outwards (8.7e4 to 1.7e4), not several times the plateau, so no hot tip: michel. 331005 (2 pts, 22 cm) sits ~11 cm off the body in x, along the Michel arm direction: gamma. 330004 (4 pts, 37 cm) is forward and below the stop, ~90 deg from the Michel direction: delta / other. A grey dotted trace (~25 cm, not in the object table) also leaves the stop at an angle with a hook; unexplained but it cannot rescue a through-going muon given the rise.

86.2 cm, enters 14 cm below the top face (y=592) and stops at x=82.5, y=525, z=331.7: 80.6 cm from the nearest face (top), 80 cm from the cathode and 101 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. The profile runs on a smooth, slightly wavy plateau of ~3-5e4 and then climbs steadily over the last ~6 cm from ~2.5e4 to ~1.2e5 at the final points, following the shape of the muon reference curve: a clear Bragg rise, peaking at the last point, so no overshoot and the pin stays. The 3.2 cm last segment 88009 (1.05e5) is the fitted muon tip. Nothing leaves the stop in any of the three azimuths and the object table has no piece other than the muon chain; f_meas shows the cluster charge ending in U, V and W with no dead band near the stop. A separate straight track runs parallel to the muon some 30-40 cm off to the side in the 3-D frames (not in the object table); it is a different object and does not touch the stop. No decay activity, no capture gamma candidates.

230 cm single-segment track, chain entry 19.3 cm below the top face at (68.3, 586.7, 360.4), stopping mid-volume at (107.8, 367.9, 368.9) in APA3, 93 cm from the nearest (back z) face, 105 cm from the cathode and 138 cm from the seam. The profile rides a ~5.5-6e4 plateau and climbs over the last ~10 cm: ~1e5 at 7-9 cm, a dip to ~6.5e4 at 4-5 cm, then 1.02e5 and 1.4e5 at the last two points, following the muon reference curve; ragged but a real rise, with no collapse after the peak (no overshoot) and nothing past the end (no hot tip, no undershoot). Charge ends cleanly in all three planes of f_meas with no dead band near the end, and nothing continues past the star in c/d/e. The object table holds only the muon: no arm, stub or speck anywhere within the drawn window, so no decay activity (consistent with mu- capture). The only thing I could not resolve is the 19 cm of missing track between the chain entry and the top face, which does not bear on the stop.

column17: mu- 33 MeV(mu- 63 MeV(mu- 547 MeV(e- 13 MeV, mu- 40 MeV(gamma 0.51 MeV(e- 0.51 MeV)))))
column19: 265 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and ending 132.4 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.3e4 plateau beyond s=40 climbing smoothly along the solid muon curve through 6.0e4 at s=20, 6.7-7.5e4 at s=10-18, 8.7-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.5-1.02e5 at s=3-4, 1.14-1.22e5 at s=1.5-2.5 and 1.39e5 at s=0.5, with the row mean for the last segment 58015 quoted at 1.05e5 over its 7.8 cm. The rise is monotone over 20 cm and the peak is at the origin, so the pin does not move and no undershoot applies (nothing sits forward of the fit end at several times MIP). Past the stop there is exactly one thing: 222018, two points spanning 0.3 cm, 9.3 cm from the stop, 7.3 cm past it and 5.7 cm off the entry-stop chord, carrying 2.0e4 e/cm and 0.5 MeV, and the chain itself records that it was bridged to the stop vertex across 9.11 cm of EMPTY space rather than by a graph edge. f_meas confirms the gap: in all three planes the speck is a single isolated brown dot at time slice 1058 with a clean charge-free break below it before the track s own hits resume at 1040. That is the rubric s attachment tie-break in its literal form -- a 0.3 cm two-point speck across a 9 cm gap is not a 35 MeV electron -- so it is a detached dot, gamma, not a michel, and the verdict stays STM_ONLY. 220017 is the second dot, two points over 4.5 cm, 41.6 cm out, 17.6 cm past the stop and 37.6 cm off the chord; I measured it at 42 degrees from 222018 as seen from the stop, i.e. on the same side of the stop as the decay charge rather than scattered in an unrelated direction, and charge is explicitly not a criterion for a faint speck at 40 cm, so gamma as well. 58010 is the one thing close and backward: 10 points over 5.5 cm, 4.0 cm back along the muon, 3.3 cm off the chord at cos_fwd -0.87, and the chain body-excludes it as pdg 11 -- that is the delta / other rule almost word for word. Two gammas and no michel gives detached dots.

85.8 cm chain in one fitted segment (52003, 145 pts, mean 56941). It enters exactly at the anode x face (d_face 0.0) and stops 37.0 cm from the z wall, 68 cm from the anode, in_fv 1. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk: the profile sits on a 4.5-6.5e4 band out beyond s = 20 and then tracks the muon reference curve point for point over the last 15 cm - 6.5e4 at s = 13, 8.0e4 at s = 8, 9.0e4 at s = 5, 1.00e5, 1.12e5, 1.18e5 and 1.23e5 at the last point - a factor of two above its own plateau, the right shape, and topping out just where the rubric says real stoppers top out. This is the one item where the chain agrees: is_stm 1. Two objects sit past the stop, and both are compact detached dots, each two points and 0.3 cm across, each drawn as an isolated marker clear of the amber body in c, d and e and each visible as a genuine isolated blob in all three f_meas planes (times 812 and 848 against the track end at 805), so they are measured charge and not fit artefacts. 93004 sits 17.6 cm out at cos_fwd +0.5 carrying 78784 e/cm and the chain independently calls it a capture gamma of 2.06 MeV; 94005 sits 11.0 cm out at cos_fwd -0.21, i.e. essentially sideways, so about 11 cm clear of the muon body line, carrying 15551 e/cm. Neither is an electron: the rubric is explicit that a 0.3 cm two-point speck across a gap of this size is not a 35 MeV electron, and there is no arm of any kind leaving the stop (n_stop_arms 0, no unfitted clusters). So both are gamma, the verdict stays STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL - isolated capture gammas do not promote it - and michel_kind is detached dots.

A downgoing 68.5 cm cosmic: it enters 0.9 cm from the top y face at y 335 and the fit end sits 45.1 cm below it, 138 cm from the anode and 137 cm from the z wall, so the stop is interior. Upscaled, the last 15 cm are a textbook rise that follows the solid muon curve and peaks at the fit's own last point: 5.4-6.3e4 at s = 13-15, 7.1-7.6e4 at s = 12, 8.1-9.2e4 at s = 7-11, 9.5-1.02e5 at s = 5-8, 1.05-1.10e5 at s = 3-5, 1.25e5 at s = 1.5 and 1.32e5 at s = 0.7 - the maximum is the final point, there is no terminal dip and no forward high-charge tip, so neither the overshoot nor the undershoot applies and the pin stays put. (The chain does have a low trough of 0.5-2e4 around s = 18-32, which is the same periodic dQ/dx pathology that earns the plateau_off_mip rejection; it is 20 cm back and does not touch the stop.) Attached at the shared stop vertex 88004 is S88008, 18 points over 10.4 cm at an 88 deg kink, mean 5.6e4 e/cm, which the chain prices at 24.5 MeV over a 32.6 cm range. A muon sitting at a 1.32e5 Bragg peak has a few tens of MeV left and cannot continue at MIP, so that arm is a second particle, and 10 cm at MIP is exactly a ~25 MeV electron: Michel. The three azimuths show it directly - a blue arm leaving the star at right angles to the amber body and running to its own vertex square, with the muon's image-point halo ending at the star. The five remaining rows are 2-3 point specks at 42-47 cm scattered around the ring in unrelated directions: S379010, S380011 and S381012 sit on the muon body line at cos_fwd -0.89, -0.87 and -0.89, while S378009 and S382013 are forward (cos_fwd +0.57 and +0.94) but lie 114 and 150 deg away from the Michel arm, i.e. on the opposite side of the stop from the decay. None is on the Michel's side, so all five are delta / other and michel_kind is attached rather than both. Charge for the muon, the arm and the specks is real in U, V and W, and U and W are clear of dead bands at the stop.

column17: mu- 352 MeV(mu- 28 MeV(mu- 50 MeV(e- 36 MeV)), e- 17 MeV)
mu- 239 MeV(gamma 14 MeV(e- 14 MeV), e- 9.63 MeV)
column19: A 94.3 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 46.0 cm from the nearest face, in_fv 1, and the chain already accepts it (is_stm 1). The Bragg is textbook and needs no argument: 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=50 to s=100, 6.5-7.5e4 at s=15-20, 7.5-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.4-9.8e4 at s=3-7, 1.07-1.11e5 at s=2 and 1.23-1.25e5 at the last two points, sitting on the solid muon curve the whole way up and topping out squarely in the 1.2-1.35e5 band. There is no terminal dip at all - the two highest points in the whole profile are the last two - so the pin stays put and neither failure mode is in play here. Past the stop a three-piece arm leaves at roughly a right angle to the muon: 79009 (11 points, 5.9 cm, 9.1e3 e/cm, d 0.0-3.41, cos_fwd -0.35) attached at the fit end, then 79011 (10 points, 5.5 cm, 4.1e4, d 2.41-7.28, cos_fwd -0.04) and 79012 (8 points, 4.0 cm, 2.3e4, d 7.28-10.62, cos_fwd -0.02), about 10.6 cm of charge at 0.17-0.76 of MIP. All three azimuths show it as a green-then-yellow chain of segments running away from the star through its own vertex squares, at a large angle to the muon and nowhere near hugging its body - cos_fwd near zero is perpendicular, not the -0.85-and-below that the delta rule wants - and it is inside 10 cm where the rubric says direction does not discriminate anyway. Attached, well clear of the body, sub-MIP: michel. A muon that has just put 1.25e5 into its last centimetre cannot carry on at a fifth to three quarters of MIP for another 10 cm. Then 180014, a 2-point 0.6 cm speck at 4.6e4 sitting 18.7-19.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.26, which in the c and d azimuths lies beyond the far end of the arm and roughly along its direction, across a clear charge-free gap - isolated, compact, past the stop, inside 60 cm, clear of the body and on the Michel's own side, so gamma, and that gives kind both. I am overriding the chain's gamma body exclusion label on it, which the rubric explicitly permits when off-axis separation says otherwise. The last object, 179013, is a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 60.1 cm out at cos_fwd +0.19, flagged survey only and never offered to either stage; it is at the very edge of the 60 cm ring, its polar angle differs from the arm's by about 0.45 in cos_fwd, and in the c azimuth it sits on the opposite side of the stop from the arm, so I read it as an unrelated speck on the ring rather than part of this decay: delta / other. f_meas is clean - the stop is at U 3600, V 7370, W 12200 with the dead lines 30-40 channels off in U and V, and measured minus predicted is flat along the track.

column17: mu- 267 MeV(e- 17 MeV, gamma 7.09 MeV(e- 7.09 MeV))
column19: Short 107 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face at (275,-310,298) and ending at (179,-302,277), 21.1 cm from the nearest (z) wall - contained, if not by much. The dQ/dx panel at 4x is a textbook Bragg peak: the chain sits at 5.4e4 out beyond s=40, 6e4 at s=20, 7-8.5e4 over s=5-15, 1.04e5 at s=2 and 1.18-1.25e5 at the last two points, riding the overlaid muon curve the whole way, and the maximum of the whole profile IS the last fit point, so there is no terminal collapse and nothing to move the pin for; range KE 267 MeV against MCS 264 MeV agrees. Leaving that vertex is a real arm: 82009 (9 points, 5.0 cm, d_min 0) and 82004 (6 points, 2.9 cm, out to 4.8 cm), both at cos_fwd ~0.8, i.e. about 40 deg off the muon's tangent, which the chain reads as a 39 deg kink and 17.5 MeV. Their points on the negative axis run 1.03e5 and 9.5e4 at |s| under 1 cm, then 8.6e4, 6.6e4, 6.3e4, 5.3e4, 4.9e4 and 3.75e4 by |s| = 5 - charge that FALLS steadily as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature and not the undershoot case; the muon's own peak is already inside the fit and higher (1.25e5) than anything in the arm, so the fit did not stop short. Views d and e show it directly: the amber muon band ends at the star and a short blue-teal segment with its own two vertex squares carries on downward at a visible kink. Further out along very nearly the same line lie 239007 (5 points, 2.5 cm) at 27-29 cm and 238006 (2 points, 0.8 cm, survey only) at 50 cm; all four non-muon objects share a direction to within cos 0.96 of each other, so both far pieces are on the Michel's side rather than scattered around the ring, are isolated and well clear of the muon body line, and read as gammas (the chain calls 239007 a 7.1 MeV capture gamma; 50 cm is a long way for that, and a brems photon from the decay electron fits the alignment better, but either way the tag is gamma). What made this one non-trivial is that alignment - three isolated pieces strung out to 50 cm along one direction could also be a single EM cascade - but nothing changes the verdict. Broad dead bands in U sit 40+ channels away from the stop; V and W are clear there.

A short one: 39.2 cm of chain entering 0.1 cm from the x face at (340,261,257) and ending at (323,267,225), 17.2 cm back from that same face - close to the wall but inside it, and the profile removes any doubt. The plateau is 5.5-6.5e4 (segment 80005 averages 58003 over 31.7 cm from s=8 to s=37) and from about s=10 the chain climbs straight up the muon reference curve without a single reversal: 1.17e5 at s=10, 1.24-1.26e5 at s=6, 1.36e5 at s=5, 1.43e5 at s=2.5, 1.52e5 at s=1.5 and 1.62e5 at the last point, which is the only place in my chunk where the data actually reaches the reference curve. The last fitted segment 80004 averages 128070 e/cm over its 8.2 cm, 2.2 times the plateau, so the rise is in the segment table too. There is no terminal dip of any kind, so the pin stays where the fit put it and the overshoot question does not arise; the undershoot question does not arise either, since there is no forward piece past the tip at all. Past the stop the c, d and e azimuths show the amber band running into the star and nothing beyond it - no arm, no dot, no speck. The one other row, 200006, is an 11-point 5.8 cm stub at 14178 e/cm sitting 22-25 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, and the d and e frames show it leaving the muon body sideways at that point, so it is body activity 22 cm up the track and tagged delta / other; it is nowhere near the stop and cannot bear on the kind. Michel_kind is none. The measured panels put the brightest charge in all three planes exactly at the stop end and no dead band within fifteen channels of it.

A 214.6 cm chain, 498.8 MeV by range with MCS agreeing at 467.7 (amb 0.09), entering 1.0 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 47.7 cm from the nearest (y) wall, in_fv 1; the chain accepts it as an STM. The dQ/dx panel is as clean as the best in this chunk: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=15 scattering about the flat solid muon curve, then a monotone climb that follows the curve all the way in - 6.5-7.2e4 at s=6-13, 8.9-9.3e4 at s=4-6, 1.03-1.09e5 at s=1.5-3, and 1.26e5 and 1.345e5 at the last two points, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band and hugging the reference. There is no terminal dip whatever: the highest two points in the entire profile are the two nearest the origin, so neither failure mode applies and the pin stays exactly where the fit put it. This is the only item in my chunk with no non-chain object at all - the table has two rows and both are the muon's own fitted segments, 80002 spanning d 0-127.65 and 80005 spanning 127.65-201.16, both at cos_fwd about -1.0 as body segments must be. All three stop azimuths show the amber flow band running to the star and stopping there with nothing drawn beyond it: no arm, no dot, no speck, and no image-point halo past the end. The chain reports the same - n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring, 0 unfitted clusters - so there is nothing to weigh and the kind is none. f_meas is clean at the stop: it sits at U 2010, V 5805 and W 10120 with the nearest dead bands 40 to 90 channels away in every plane, and measured minus predicted is flat white along the whole track, so the Bragg is measured, not inferred.
